1:1.targetText: The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth!

1:5.sourceText: Ἀγαπητέ, πιστὸν ποιεῖς ὃ ἐὰν ἐργάσῃ εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοῦτο ξένους,
1:5.targetText: Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you may do toward the brothers and the one [among] strangers,

groups.note: The Greek indefinite relative ὃ ἐάν gives whatever action is done. English recasts that relative complement under act faithfully as in whatever; it is not a separately written Greek ἐν.

review.method: Explicit phrase and occurrence review by coding assistant; pending reader verification. Text and offsets mechanically validated.

sourceNotes.reason: N1904 τοῦτο is the neuter demonstrative this, resuming the faithful action even to strangers. It does not name a personal the one among strangers, so the edition’s different demonstrative wording is not equated.

targetNotes.reason: The pinned LSV edition has this personal/demonstrative phrase. N1904 has neuter τοῦτο, this, referring to the action; the different referents are left unpaired rather than changing the English edition.

1:6.targetText: who testified of your love before an assembly, whom you will do well, having sent forward worthily of God,

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God after worthily; no separate Greek of preposition is printed.

1:7.sourceText: ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ Ὀνόματος ἐξῆλθαν μηδὲν λαμβάνοντες ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνικῶν.
1:7.targetText: because they went forth for [His] Name, receiving nothing from the nations;

groups.note: The substantive plural ἐθνικῶν refers to Gentile/outsider peoples, rendered collectively as nations; this is the actual adjective used substantivally, not a claim that the text contains the different noun ἔθνη.

1:9.sourceText: Ἔγραψά τι τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἀλλ’ ὁ φιλοπρωτεύων αὐτῶν Διοτρεφὴς οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται ἡμᾶς.
1:9.targetText: I wrote to the assembly, but he who is loving to be first among them—Diotrephes—does not receive us;

review.method: Explicit phrase and occurrence review by coding assistant; pending reader verification. Text and offsets mechanically validated.

sourceNotes.reason: The indefinite τι, something, is explicitly written with I wrote in N1904 but not separately expressed in LSV.

1:10.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο, ἐὰν ἔλθω, ὑπομνήσω αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιεῖ λόγοις πονηροῖς φλυαρῶν ἡμᾶς, καὶ μὴ ἀρκούμενος ἐπὶ τούτοις οὔτε αὐτὸς ἐπιδέχεται τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοὺς βουλομένους κωλύει καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐκβάλλει.
1:10.targetText: because of this, if I may come, I will cause him to remember his works that he does, talking nonsense against us with evil words; and not content with these, neither does he himself receive the brothers, and he forbids those intending [to receive them], and he casts [them] out of the assembly.

groups.note: The actual receive predicate supplies both the finite he does not receive and the understood [to receive] complement of the immediately coordinated intending people. This is the same reception action, not an independently written second verb.

The actual brothers are the direct object both of receive and of its immediately inherited [to receive them] complement. The bracketed them resumes these same brothers; it is not a separate written pronoun.

The actual substantival article names those intending to receive the brothers. These same immediately coordinated people are forbidden and cast out; the final bracketed [them] resumes that stated group, without a separate written object pronoun.

review.note: Shared complements are restricted to the actual coordinated reception/forbidding/casting relations: the receive predicate is inherited after intending; the brothers are its object; the intending people are forbidden and cast out. The earlier causative reminder recipient him remains honestly unpaired because that different recipient role is not stated in N1904.
review.method: Explicit phrase and occurrence review by coding assistant; pending reader verification. Text and offsets mechanically validated.

sourceNotes.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

targetNotes.reason: N1904 says I will call attention to his works; αὐτοῦ is the actual possessor his. LSV additionally specifies him as the recipient of causing-to-remember, a role not independently identified in the Greek reminder construction.

1:11.sourceText: Ἀγαπητέ, μὴ μιμοῦ τὸ κακὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀγαθόν. ὁ ἀγαθοποιῶν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν· ὁ κακοποιῶν οὐχ ἑώρακεν τὸν Θεόν.
1:11.targetText: Beloved, do not be following that which is evil, but that which is good; he who is doing good, he is of God, [but] he who is doing evil has not seen God;

1:12.targetText: testimony has been given to Demetrius by all, and by the truth itself, and we also—we testify, and you have known that our testimony is true.

1:13.sourceText: Πολλὰ εἶχον γράψαι σοι, ἀλλ’ οὐ θέλω διὰ μέλανος καὶ καλάμου σοι γράφειν·
1:13.targetText: Many things I had to write, but I do not wish to write to you through ink and pen,

groups.note: Greek explicitly gives the same recipient σοι in both coordinated writing clauses. English expresses that common writing recipient once, after the second to write; the two actual dative identities are condensed into this single final to you.

1:14.sourceText: ἐλπίζω δὲ εὐθέως σε ἰδεῖν, καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλήσομεν.
1:14.targetText: and I hope to see you soon, and we will speak mouth to mouth. Peace to you! The friends greet you. Be greeting the friends by name.

review.note: The Greek witness has a separate closing greeting at 1:15; this translation joins it to 1:14. The original witness reference and wording remain unchanged.

1:3.sourceText: ἐχάρην γὰρ λίαν ἐρχομένων ἀδελφῶν καὶ μαρτυρούντων σου τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, καθὼς σὺ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ περιπατεῖς.
1:3.targetText: for I rejoiced exceedingly, brothers coming and testifying of the truth in you, even as you walk in truth;

groups.note: The Greek genitive σου qualifies the attested truth as your truth; LSV expresses the same person/truth relationship as truth in you, not as a separately written Greek ἐν preposition.
